label: Pule
note: Needs goat milk: donkey milk has too little casein, especially kappa-casein, for rennet to set it alone. About 25 L of milk per kg; only a few dozen jennies are milked, by hand.

about.text: Pule, or magareći sir, is a Serbian cheese made from 60 % Balkan donkey milk and 40 % goat milk at the Zasavica nature reserve. It is crumbly and reported to taste like manchego, and is among the most expensive cheeses because so little milk is available.

sources.text: The first paragraph of its article, shortened.

how.text: Pure donkey milk set with calf rennet only under extreme conditions in a University of Bari trial (5.9 % yield, soft curd); 15–30 % goat milk improved coagulation, which is why pule is blended.

steps.note: The curds are strained, then packed in moulds, much as for a young rindless chèvre.
Up to 3 days in the mould.
